content: Key-layout conventions for CID-addressed data: kubo stores raw blocks in flatfs — flat files in sharded directories using prefix/suffix/next-to-last sharding of the upper-case base32 multihash; flatfs is explicitly content-addressed-only with first-successful-writer-wins semantics (safe because identical keys guarantee identical values) and restricts keys to base32 with no namespaces; boxo blockstore namespaces a /blocks prefix over a datastore and keys by multihash; versioned top-level prefixes (v1/blocks/, v1/cars/) are a common bucket hygiene convention letting layout evolve without migration; s5 uses blob3/ prefixes for packed blobs and .tmp/ for in-flight writes. Prefix fan-out mainly benefits filesystem dirs and S3 listing/audit operations; pure GET/HEAD by full key does not need it.
